newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat rises on tight supply, Europe concern.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat rises on tight supply, Europe concern.

text.p: Australian wheat futures rose strongly on Friday on local tight supply and the European Union's closure of weekly export tenders for 1996/97 wheat.
Two contracts traded a total of seven lots on the Sydney Futures Exchange, with July 1997 up A$3.50 to A$193.00 on the trade and January 1998 up A$6.50 to A$188.00.

Settlement prices rose almost across-the-board, with the two nearest-term contracts down A$1.50 each but the mid-term contracts of November 1997 and January 1998 up by A$7.00 and A$7.50 respectively. More distant contracts rose by A$4.00-A$6.00 a tonne.
"The domestic marketing situation has become quite serious now that the AWB has sold the majority of the 1996 crop," said Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures.
"And we now have a situation where Europe has declared it will not export any wheat because it is worried about the current drought it is having," he said.
The Australian domestic market would be squeezed as it scrambled for the little wheat that was left, he said.
Lindsay believes the market will rise briskly toward A$200.00/A$210.00 a tonne in the May and January contracts.
AWB multigrade 1997/98 indicators rose A$6.00 on Friday.
